judgeRationales.scenarioName: Catches compound allocations in recursive number converter with ToLower
judgeRationales.rationale: Both miss the required 8+ call count and include some unsupported or distracting claims, but B more clearly recognizes the central compound `+=`/interpolation/lowercasing allocation pattern and quantifies the per-line cost. A is clearer on invariant casing and marginally closer on the count, making the overall gap modest.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Detects Aggregate+Replace chain and struct missing IEquatable
judgeRationales.rationale: B directly and accurately covers four of the five requested observations, with code/location evidence and a positive FrozenDictionary finding. A covers the Replace-chain and IEquatable points but misses the per-iteration char.ToString allocation and FrozenDictionary positive, while adding less substantiated unrelated estimates.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Detects CurrentCulture comparer and compiled regex budget in inflection rules
judgeRationales.rationale: A delivers all requested core performance observations with concrete implementation details and recommendations; B only asks the user to provide the code and does not answer the task.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Finds StringComparison.Ordinal missing and FrozenDictionary opportunities
judgeRationales.rationale: B meets all requested findings with more actionable locations and examples, while A makes the substantive prohibited error of treating the mutable Hungarian runtime cache as a FrozenDictionary-related issue. Both include some unsupported performance estimates, but this does not overturn B's stronger rubric performance.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Finds branched Replace chain in format string manipulation
judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: B, reverse: A). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Finds hot-path allocations in string humanization
judgeRationales.rationale: B is more accurate about the existing regex optimizations, clearer and more structured, and uniquely preserves the important span-based positive finding. Both cover several core hot-path issues but both miss the required Dehumanize string.Concat(words.Select(...)) finding and fail to clearly call out ToLower's string allocation; B's unsupported GC estimate and terse final recommendations prevent a larger margin.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Finds per-call Dictionary allocation not hoisted to static
judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: B, reverse: A). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Finds repeated enumeration in time and collection formatting
judgeRationales.rationale: Both runs identify most required hotspots and leave the fixture unchanged. B is more precise for SetPrecisionOfTimeSpan and the object overload, but its final response omits the required Reverse finding and largely points to external deliverables instead of presenting the recommendations. A directly presents all major requested categories, including Reverse, although its materialization discussion and quantitative claims are less well substantiated.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Flags Span inconsistencies and compound method chains in truncation library
judgeRationales.rationale: B provides a substantially more actionable review and directly covers the Symbols/List<char>[] rubric item, while also recognizing the FixedLength allocation issue. Both miss the precise Span-consistency observation, and B's shown ReadOnlySpan<char>[] declaration is questionable in C#, so its advantage is real but limited.

judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: B, reverse: A). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: B, reverse: A). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: .NET Framework on Windows without admin privileges
judgeRationales.rationale: B closely follows all core .NET Framework guidance: PerfView/admin necessity, no trace fallback, dotnet-trace incompatibility, and dump limitations. A contains material inaccuracies on the central limitations, especially suggesting non-admin tracing/profiling paths and denying non-admin dump capture.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Assembly loading failure on Linux (.NET 8)
judgeRationales.rationale: B directly answers the core tracing question with the correct assembly-loader event command and a startup-safe launch form. However, its explicit erroneous `collect-linux` recommendation is a significant flaw for .NET 8, preventing a stronger overall verdict. A avoids that bad command but largely fails to answer the requested tracing workflow.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Container installation without .NET SDK
judgeRationales.rationale: B directly answers the central no-SDK scenario with a working aka.ms download and curl command plus container injection/collection steps. A omits the requested standalone-download method and includes questionable or less applicable alternatives. Both miss kubectl cp.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Excessive GC on Linux (.NET 8)
judgeRationales.rationale: B satisfies the task's central, version-appropriate recommendation and exact gc-verbose command, while A misses both and includes confusing/misleading format and analysis instructions. Both omit the explicit trace-versus-dump explanation, but B is otherwise substantially more correct and actionable.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: HTTP 500s from downstream service on Linux (.NET 8)
judgeRationales.rationale: B directly answers the operational question with a networking-provider dotnet-trace collection command and explains status-code and duration analysis. A remains high-level and defers the requested command, so it is materially less useful despite covering generic HTTP tracing and timing.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Hang or deadlock diagnosis on Linux
judgeRationales.rationale: B follows the requested trace-first, dump-if-unexplained diagnostic flow and clearly classifies the principal hang modes. A has useful generic triage commands, but misses the requested causal workflow and distinctions. Both omit the lldb/SOS dump-analysis guidance. [Magnitude reduced to "slightly-better": the position-swapped pass judged this "slightly-better", so the more confident "much-better" was downgraded.]

judgeRationales.scenarioName: High CPU in Kubernetes on Linux (.NET 8)
judgeRationales.rationale: B delivers the requested Kubernetes-specific, executable dotnet-trace workflow, including direct download, collection, retrieval, and analysis, and correctly situates .NET 8. Its copy path could be made more robust by specifying an output path during collection, and it omits dotnet-monitor, but it substantially covers more of the rubric than A.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Kubernetes with console access prefers console tools
judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: A, reverse: B). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Linux pre-.NET 10 needing native call stacks
judgeRationales.rationale: B directly answers the version-specific need with usable perfcollect installation and collection commands and avoids the incorrect .NET 8 dotnet-trace-native-stack advice. It omits an explicit statement that dotnet-trace is managed-only and only implies the root requirement through sudo, but it is still substantially more correct and complete than A.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Long-running intermittent issue with PerfView triggers
judgeRationales.rationale: B directly answers the unattended-capture request with a coherent circular-buffer command, CPU symptom trigger, and timing guidance. A contains relevant options but its recommended setup lacks automatic stopping and its trigger suggestion is manual and disconnected, so it does not reliably solve the stated problem.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Memory leak on .NET Framework Windows
judgeRationales.rationale: B directly and concisely covers every requested diagnostic action: two ProcDump captures during growth, a PerfView allocation trace, PerfView dump diffing, and collection before failure. A has a valid ProcDump recommendation and useful ancillary suggestions, but misses the key explicit PerfView diff/allocation guidance and is less focused on the requested collection plan.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Memory leak on Linux (.NET 8)
judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: tie, reverse: A). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Networking timeouts on Windows with admin (.NET 8)
judgeRationales.rationale: B closely follows the requested diagnostic strategy and covers all core providers and trace interpretation. A offers generic alternatives and troubleshooting suggestions but misses the central PerfView/thread-time solution entirely.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Slow requests on Windows with PerfView
judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: B, reverse: A). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Windows container high CPU with PerfView
judgeRationales.rationale: B supplies the central requested solution—host-side PerfView collection with /EnableEventsInContainers—and usable collection guidance. It is incomplete on symbol merging/off-machine analysis, but A misses the core Windows-container PerfView workflow entirely.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Windows modern .NET with admin high CPU
judgeRationales.rationale: B cleanly fulfills all three requested rubric points with a concise PerfView-first workflow, command, output, and analysis guidance. A is generally diagnostic advice but answers with the wrong preferred tool and misses the requested PerfView collection command.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Advisory: CoreCLR Alpine Docker non-root configuration
judgeRationales.rationale: B directly covers all requested configuration elements with modern variables, SYS_PTRACE, and secure non-root directory ownership. A omits SYS_PTRACE, uses only legacy variable names with one inaccurate type description, and introduces unwarranted Alpine-specific concern.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Advisory: NativeAOT Kubernetes dump collection setup
judgeRationales.rationale: B directly satisfies every required .NET 11 NativeAOT configuration item with a coherent pod example. A gets the capability and storage concepts but uses incorrect environment-variable names and a wrong mechanism for the createdump path, which undermines the core setup.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Advisory: macOS NativeAOT crash dump recovery steps
judgeRationales.rationale: B directly covers the two recovery locations, makes the crucial pre-crash `ulimit -c unlimited` condition clear, and avoids analysis of an existing dump. A misses the explicit `/cores` recovery check and pre-crash ulimit requirement and adds prohibited lldb analysis; its no-tool trajectory advantage does not outweigh these core omissions.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Configure CoreCLR dump collection in Alpine Docker as non-root
judgeRationales.rationale: B satisfies the two core explicit requirements A misses: the DOTNET-prefixed enable variable and SYS_PTRACE. It also supplies complete Dockerfile and run examples with non-root dump-directory handling. A has useful ownership guidance but its command omits the required capability and uses only legacy COMPlus settings.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Configure automatic crash dumps for CoreCLR app on Linux
judgeRationales.rationale: Both satisfy every requested configuration item. B is marginally more actionable because its required variables are shown as shell exports in one ready-to-use block and its path placeholders are presented correctly. A has the stronger running-process verification, but also makes a misleading description of `%e` and shows bare rather than exported assignments.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Decline dump analysis request
judgeRationales.rationale: B directly communicates the required out-of-scope limitation and performs no dump access or analysis. Although it inconsistently offers to guide future analysis, it is materially more compliant than A, which asserts it can analyze the dump and starts checking for dump files. [Magnitude reduced to "slightly-better": the position-swapped pass judged this "slightly-better", so the more confident "much-better" was downgraded.]

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Detect runtime and configure crash dumps for unknown .NET app on Linux
judgeRationales.rationale: B is safer and more methodical: it uses the appropriate binary-inspection approach, verifies the inaccessible PID, avoids making a runtime assumption, and does not drift into analysis. A is more immediately useful with conditional configuration, but its detection guidance is weak and it violates the no-analysis requirement.

Response B's proactive tool use (searching for .dmp files) is more egregious than Response A's passive promise without action.

judgeRationales.rationale: B is substantially more concrete and source-grounded about the compound interpolation/`+=` allocation issue, including exact sites and a useful rewrite. Both miss the required 8+ lowercase-site count, and both include some questionable allocation claims, so the overall advantage is limited rather than large.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Detects compiled regex startup budget and regex chain allocations
judgeRationales.rationale: B covers all requested findings, including the decisive Underscore Replace allocation chain and the positive GeneratedRegex practice, with a more focused final analysis. A misses those two rubric-critical items in its delivered result and includes dubious, highly specific allocation/GC estimates and an incorrect lazy-compilation explanation. [Magnitude reduced to "slightly-better": the position-swapped pass judged this "slightly-better", so the more confident "much-better" was downgraded.]

judgeRationales.rationale: A is incomplete—it stops short of the explicit symbol-server explanation and concrete recovery paths—but it correctly identifies the limitation and avoids false symbolication. judgeRationales.rationale: B provides the key NativeAOT-specific symbol ownership and symbol-server guidance, with appropriate limits on what can actually be resolved. A's claimed symbolication is fabricated from address heuristics and makes unsupported causal/function claims, so it is materially unreliable despite recognizing NativeAOT.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Reject iOS crash log as wrong format
judgeRationales.rationale: Both satisfy every rubric requirement and correctly decline Android symbolication. B is modestly stronger because it actually inspects and cites the log's unsymbolicated MyApp addresses and gives a concrete dSYM requirement; A is otherwise correct but unnecessarily refers to the evaluation scenario.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Symbolicate .NET frames in an Android tombstone
judgeRationales.rationale: B follows the proper symbol-server and llvm-symbolizer workflow and delivers a concrete, source-located backtrace. A only reports an unsupported, incorrect-looking function list and omits the required URL, command, and source locations.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Symbolicate CoreCLR frames in an Android tombstone
judgeRationales.rationale: B directly fulfills every requested symbolication-oriented rubric item, including the actionable symbol download URL and symbolizer invocations. A has the BuildId and a CoreCLR characterization but omits the required URL and commands, while making unsupported crash-cause assertions instead of presenting usable symbolication steps.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Symbolicate tombstone with multiple .NET libraries and different BuildIds
judgeRationales.rationale: B follows the BuildId-based workflow: it parses the frames, constructs all distinct URLs, attempts and validates downloads, and provides concrete symbolizer commands. judgeRationales.scenarioName: Advisory: CoreCLR Alpine Docker non-root configuration
judgeRationales.rationale: Response B is slightly better overall because it provides more practical, actionable guidance that directly addresses the user's configuration needs. It excels at criterion 4 (explicitly stating Alpine needs no workarounds) and criterion 3 (providing concrete setup steps). While Response A is significantly stronger on criterion 2 (deeper technical understanding of SYS_PTRACE requirements), Response B better balances technical accuracy with practical usability. For someone implementing crash dump collection in Alpine Docker containers, Response B provides clearer direction (host setup steps, verification commands, version considerations), while Response A provides deeper technical context that would benefit someone needing to understand security policy interactions. The explicit upfront statement about Alpine needs and the practical setup guidance give Response B an edge for answering the question as posed."

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Configure CoreCLR dump collection in Alpine Docker as non-root
judgeRationales.rationale: Both responses correctly address all rubric criteria. However, Response A provides a more robust technical solution for the specific constraint of non-root user operation by using setcap to grant file capabilities to the createdump binary. This is the more reliable approach for non-root dump collection. Response B is simpler and more maintainable with better documentation (verification commands, cleanup notes), but its technical approach of relying solely on container-level SYS_PTRACE capability may not be sufficient for non-root user operations in all scenarios. Given that the task explicitly emphasizes non-root operation, Response A's more thorough handling of this constraint gives it a slight edge in quality."

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Catches compound allocations in recursive number converter with ToLower
judgeRationales.rationale: B directly covers the key allocation mechanism, the embedded +=/interpolation anti-pattern, and correctly identifies the eight active recursive lowercasing sites. A misses those central specifics and gives an incorrect count, despite sharing the general StringBuilder and invariant-culture recommendations.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Detects Aggregate+Replace chain and struct missing IEquatable
judgeRationales.rationale: B identifies the central Aggregate/Replace allocation problem and, importantly, the per-iteration char.ToString allocation that A entirely misses. Its result is less speculative and its generated optimization also addresses structural equality. Both miss the requested short-circuit recommendation and an explicit positive FrozenDictionary finding. [Magnitude reduced to "slightly-better": the position-swapped pass judged this "slightly-better", so the more confident "much-better" was downgraded.]

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Detects CurrentCulture comparer and compiled regex budget in inflection rules
judgeRationales.rationale: Both satisfy all requested findings. B is marginally stronger because it gives clearer code locations, directly connects both registration methods to the constructor, and offers a concrete comparer replacement. Its extra FrozenDictionary discussion and both responses' unbenchmarked timing claims do not materially improve the core answer.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Detects compiled regex startup budget and regex chain allocations
judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: B, reverse: A). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Finds StringComparison.Ordinal missing and FrozenDictionary opportunities
judgeRationales.rationale: B delivers a clear review that covers all required findings, including the Swedish ordinal-comparison issue and allocation-heavy concatenation. A misses or only ambiguously addresses those two required areas and presents an implementation-style summary rather than a complete performance review.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Finds branched Replace chain in format string manipulation
judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: B, reverse: A). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Finds hot-path allocations in string humanization
judgeRationales.rationale: Both capture several central hot-path allocation issues and leave the fixture unchanged, but B covers all requested performance targets, including the Dehumanize Concat/Select cost and the positive span-based helper finding, with substantially more actionable recommendations. Its extra speculative claims and inflated estimates prevent a larger margin.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Finds per-call Dictionary allocation not hoisted to static
judgeRationales.rationale: B is substantially more useful as a performance review: it names both affected converters, explains the allocation mechanisms, provides locations and concrete remediation. A appears to have applied fixes, including the otherwise omitted FormatWithUnit issue, but its final report is too terse and makes unsubstantiated performance/allocation claims. B's omission of the fifth required finding prevents a larger advantage.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Finds repeated enumeration in time and collection formatting
judgeRationales.rationale: Position-swap inconsistent (forward: A, reverse: B). Defaulting to tie.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Flags Span inconsistencies and compound method chains in truncation library
judgeRationales.rationale: B more explicitly and accurately surfaces the first two requested hot-path findings, with locations and a correct fix for the TrimEnd chain. A is safer on the Symbols recommendation, while B's span-array sample is invalid, so the overall advantage is narrow rather than large.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Identifies unsealed leaf classes and locale hierarchy patterns
judgeRationales.rationale: Both miss the required StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase positive finding and otherwise cover the principal sealing recommendation. B is marginally clearer on the class count, but its review introduces several unsupported and implausibly precise performance claims (2–5x, ~25x, and 15–25% gains) plus speculative secondary advice. A is more focused and less misleading overall, despite its count wording inconsistency and an unsubstantiated smaller estimate.

judgeRationales.scenarioName: Symbolicate CoreCLR frames in an Android tombstone
